# Root Cause Analysis

`customer_support.diagnosis_and_resolution.root_cause_analysis` · v1.0.0 · **draft**

**What condition makes this system do the wrong thing, and does that explanation survive the cases where it does not happen?**


> Working backwards from what a customer could see to the condition that made the system behave wrongly, and stating that condition so precisely that someone else could reproduce it, argue with it, or prove it wrong. The discipline is subtractive rather than accumulative: it is the business of eliminating explanations, and it ends not when a plausible story exists but when the remaining story survives the cases that do NOT show the symptom. Its output is a claim about a system — a missing guardrail, an unvalidated input, an untested path, a decision taken without the information that would have changed it — and never a claim about a person. Root cause analysis is also the capability that holds the difference between closing a ticket and closing an issue, because it is the only place in the support motion where anybody is looking at the fault rather than at the queue.

## Expertise applied


## Outcomes

- A named mechanism: the condition under which the system does the wrong thing, written so a stranger to the ticket could make it happen on purpose.
- A causal chain that terminates in something the organisation owns and can change — a control, a default, a validation, a process — and never in a person's name.
- Blast radius established: every ticket carrying this symptom attached to one issue, so the size of the problem is a fact rather than an impression formed from whichever tickets were loudest.
- The two closures separated and both recorded: what stopped the customer's pain, and what stopped the fault. Where only the first happened, the issue is left explicitly open with an owner.
- A cannot-reproduce finding where the fault will not surface — carrying the classes of cause it eliminated and the conditions that were ruled out, which is a result and not a closure.
- An accepted-unknown verdict where the investigation is stopped deliberately, naming the evidence that would justify reopening it.
- A statement of what would have caught this earlier, handed to whoever owns that surface — tests, monitoring, validation, onboarding, documentation.


## Failure modes

- Fixing the symptom. The error is suppressed, the ticket closes green, and the same fault surfaces next quarter wearing different words and gets investigated from scratch.
- Stopping at the first true thing. 'The disk filled' is true, is not why the disk filled, and is satisfying enough to end most investigations.
- Naming a person. 'The agent applied the wrong configuration' identifies who was standing nearest the failure, not why the system accepted a wrong configuration. It cannot be fixed, only punished, and the next person does the same thing.
- Treating cannot-reproduce as a close reason rather than a finding. It collapses environmental, intermittent, state-dependent and misdescribed faults into one bin and discards the only information the failed reproduction gave you.
- Root-causing the ticket instead of the issue. The fastest way to spend a week on a defect that affected one account while the one affecting forty stays unlabelled.
- Declaring the cause because the fix worked. A restart makes almost anything stop and proves nothing whatsoever about why it started.
- Letting the workaround end the analysis. The ticket goes green, the issue record goes quiet, and the only remaining evidence that the product is broken is a memory in one agent's head that leaves with them.
- Analysis written after the decision. An RCA produced to justify a fix already shipped is documentation, and everyone in the review knows it.
- Confusing a trigger with a cause. The customer's bulk import did not cause the failure; it was simply the first thing large enough to reach it, and blaming the import means the next large thing finds it again.
- Convicting the deploy because the deploy is the only change anyone timestamps. Correlation with a release is the strongest signal available and still routinely convicts the innocent.
- Investigating alone. The person who wrote the subsystem can eliminate half the hypothesis space in one sentence, and support's reluctance to spend that sentence is expensive.
- Perfect analysis, no communication. The customer's experience of a rigorous silent investigation is indistinguishable from being ignored.
- One cause declared where several are contributing. Once the first is found the search stops, and the remaining ones resurface as 'the fix did not work'.


## KPIs

| KPI | Unit | Direction | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| root_cause_identified_rate | percent | higher_is_better | Share of issues reaching a named mechanism rather than closing on user error, cannot reproduce, or no fault found. |
| time_to_root_cause | days | lower_is_better | From issue opened to mechanism named. Measured on the issue, never on the ticket, or a workaround shipped fast will read as an investigation done fast. |
| recurrence_after_fix_rate | percent | lower_is_better | Issues that resurface after being closed as fixed. The only honest test of whether the cause was the cause. |
| cannot_reproduce_conversion_rate | percent | higher_is_better | Share of cannot-reproduce findings later resolved into a named cause. Tells you whether the finding is being used as a branch or as a bin. |
| human_error_attribution_rate | percent | lower_is_better | Share of causes terminating on a person or a role. Any sustained reading is a statement about the analysis rather than about the staff. |
| ticket_to_issue_linkage_rate | percent | higher_is_better | Share of tickets attached to an issue record. Blast radius is unmeasurable below this, and so is every prioritisation decision built on it. |
| workaround_only_issue_age | days | lower_is_better | How long issues sit closed at the ticket and open at the fault. The debt this capability is uniquely positioned to see and the queue is structurally unable to. |
| issues_per_root_cause | ratio | target_band | How many separately reported issues collapse into one underlying cause. Rising is usually good — it means analysis is reaching deep enough to unify. |

> Contains no numbers by design — no severity bands, no time-boxes, no confidence scores. Those belong to the pack manifest at Layer 4, and this file is the judgement that decides which of them are worth computing. Two things to watch in review. First, the load-set here requires issue and root_cause and treats ticket as optional, which is deliberate and will look wrong: this capability analyses the fault, and a ticket is one report of it. Second, every signal this capability would most like to read — reproduction_failed, root_cause_identified, ticket_reopened — is planned substrate rather than shipped substrate, so nothing here routes automatically yet. That is the Layer 1/2 backlog, and it is stated rather than papered over.
